title: Length-loop entry from multiplication
statement: Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, and $\sigma$ a register state whose fifteen values are at most $B$. Suppose its scratch-sum, scratch-product, and walk-length values are all zero, and $100n^4+10n\le B$, where $n$ is its vertex-count value. Assume that for every $a,b\le B$, the program started at $w0$ on input $x$, with the row and inner counters set to $a,b$, the scratch-sum set to $10n$, the scratch-product set to $n(10n)$, and the walk length set to $n(10n)(n(10n))$ (all other values unchanged), has all live register values at most $B$, terminates along every sequence of choices, and has acceptance probability $q$ and rejection probability $1-q$ for every choice length at which every sequence of choices halts. Then the program started at $lc(0)$ from $\sigma$ has those same bounded-register termination and probability properties.
hypotheses_covered: $\sigma$ is a register state bounded by $B$
scratch-sum, scratch-product, and walk-length values are zero
for every $a,b\le B$, the specified state at $w0$ has bounded-register probabilistic semantics $q$
replaced:
Let $B$ be a natural-number bound, $q$ a rational number, and $\sigma$ a 15-register
state whose registers are all at most $B$. Suppose its scratch-sum, scratch-product, and
walk-length registers satisfy $\sigma.e=\sigma.f=\sigma.L=0$, and
$100\sigma.n^4+10\sigma.n\le B$. If, for every $a,b\le B$, the randomized program
$\mathrm{upA}$ on input $x$, started at label $w0$ with the registers of $\sigma$ except
that the row and inner counters are $a,b$, the scratch-sum register is $10\sigma.n$, the
scratch-product register is $\sigma.n(10\sigma.n)$, and the walk-length register is
$\sigma.n(10\sigma.n)(\sigma.n(10\sigma.n))$, has acceptance probability $q$, then the
same program started at label $lc(0)$ with state $\sigma$ has acceptance probability
$q$.
